entities.summary: Georg Tannstetter, also called Georgius Collimitius, was a humanist teaching at the University of Vienna. He was a medical doctor, mathematician, astronomer, cartographer, and the personal physician of the emperors Maximilian I and Ferdinand I. He also wrote under the pseudonym of "Lycoripensis". His Latin name "Collimitius" is derived from limes meaning "border" and is a reference to his birth town: "Rain" is a German word for border or boundary. Georg Tannstetter was a logicians & mathematicians from Rain (1482-04-01, Rain–1535-04-15). Recognized as a landmark figure with global significance (referenced in 0 Wikipedia editions). Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a personal physician to emperors Maximilian I and Ferdinand I, Georg Tannstetter had significant regional impact through his medical expertise and cartographic work. His writings under the pseudonym 'Lycoripensis' reflect his contributions to logic and mathematics.
